Diseases transmitted from the colon, rectum and anus.  
The challenge of the 90s.  
Over the past two decades, there has been an explosive growth in the prevalence and types of sexually transmitted diseases.  
Up to 55 percent of gay men with anorectal disorders have gonorrhea; 80 percent of syphilis patients are homosexuals.  
Chlamydia is present in 15 percent of gay men, and up to a third of gay men have active anorectal herpes simplex virus.  
In addition, a multitude of parasites, bacterial, viral and protozoa, are rife in the homosexual population.  
Additionally, the AIDS epidemic has produced a plethora of colorectal manifestations.  
Acute cytomegalovirus ileocolitis is the most common indication for emergency abdominal surgery in homosexual men with AIDS.  
In addition to cryptosporidia and isospora, the patient may present to the colorectal surgeon with bloody diarrhea and weight loss before diagnosis of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) disease.  
Other patients may have Kaposi's colorectal sarcoma or anorectal lymphoma and will therefore be HIV positive.  
However, in addition to protean manifestations, a third of AIDS patients consult the colorectal surgeon either for condyloma acuminatum, or for anorectal septicemia, or for proctitis before the diagnosis of HIV disease.  
Although anorectal surgery is associated with reasonable surgical outcomes in some asymptomatic HIV-positive patients, the same procedures in AIDS patients (symptomatic HIV-positive) will often produce disastrous results.  
It is therefore the responsibility of the surgeon to recognize the manifestations of HIV disease and diagnose these conditions accordingly.

Does carotid restenosis predict increased risk of symptoms, stroke or death?  
The identification of carotid restenosis as a late complication of carotid endarterectomy has raised concerns about its significance as a source of new brain symptoms, stroke, and death.  
To investigate these concerns, we analyzed a series of 507 patients undergoing 566 carotid endarteries, each documented as satisfactory.  
Data from postoperative duplex Doppler examination at 3 days, 1, 3, 6, 12 months, then annually in 484 arteries (85.5%) made it possible to classify these arteries according to the most severe degree of stenosis: normal (n = 306); 1% to 19% (n = 89); 20% to 50% (n = 40); more than 50% (n = 49, including 8 occluded).  
The 50% incidence of restenosis was 14.5% in women and 7.7% in men (p = 0.003).  
Life table analyzes up to 10 years revealed a longer life expectancy in those with restenosis (p = 0.05).  
Strokes were less likely in patients with restenosis, although this difference was not statistically significant.  
When survival and stroke were endpoints, the probability of patients with restenosis greater than 50% remaining alive and stroke-free was greater than that of the group with stenosis less than 20% (p = 0.03).  
Thus, patients with carotid restenosis were less likely than patients with normal postoperative examinations to experience symptoms, stroke, or early death.

source: Thrombolysis and angioplasty in the management of coagulated hemodialysis grafts: early and late clinical results. Pharmacomechanical thrombolysis and angioplasty outcomes of 121 thrombosed hemodialysis grafts were reviewed. The initial pharmacomechanical method (used in 65 cases) used maceration of the clot with hook-shaped catheters and lacing of the clot with highly concentrated urokinase. The current technique (used in 56 cases) consisted of a pulsed spray injection of urokinase into the clot. All fully treated grafts (117 cases) underwent complete or near-complete thrombolysis, and 93% remained patent after 1 day. The average pulse spray lysis time was 46 minutes +/- 21. One patient (less than 1%) had a gastrointestinal hemorrhage and received a transfusion; minor complications occurred in 3% of patients. The primary and secondary graft patency rates for the two methods at 1 year were 26% and 51%, respectively. Although graft age and angioplasty outcomes did not influence future graft patency, shorter intervals between graft thromboses were predictive of subsequent graft failure. The results suggest that pharmacomechanical thrombolysis and angioplasty provide rapid, consistent, and safe recanalization of coagulated hemodialysis grafts and represent an additional therapeutic approach for long-term graft management.

source: Doppler diagnosis of mechanical prosthetic mitral regurgitation: usefulness of the flow convergence region proximal to the regurgitant orifice. In addition, we studied 33 patients with mitral prostheses. Doppler studies were performed in the apical, subcostal, and parasternal axis views. FCR was detected in % (19 of 20) of patients with mitral regurgitation. A jet zone in the left atrium was detected in 60% (12 of 20) of patients. In 18 of 19 patients with Doppler-detected FCR, the leak site was identified by observing the location of the FCR. source: Invasive diagnosis of right extracardiac conduit obstruction by combined magnetic resonance imaging and continuous-wave Doppler echocardiography. The right-sided extracardiac conduits frequently become obstructed over time. We compared the utility of two-dimensional and Doppler echocardiography and magnetic resonance imaging in the diagnosis of right-sided obstruction with cardiac catheterization and angiography in 10 patients with xenograft or homograft conduits. The correlation (r = 0.95) between continuous wave Doppler estimates and catheter withdrawal pressure gradients across the conduits was excellent. Echocardiography was only able to visualize five of the ten conduits in their entirety. Magnetic resonance imaging visualized all conduits and showed statistically significant agreement (kappa = 0.58) with angiography in localizing and estimating the severity of a variety of right-sided obstructions in these patients. However, flow voids created by the metal ring around the xenograft valves led to a false-negative diagnosis of valve stenosis in four patients when magnetic resonance imaging was used alone. Doppler studies correctly indicated obstruction in these patients. source: Sodium hypertension and sodium retention. The differences between sodium hypertension and sodium hypertension were theoretically examined using a water reservoir model of regulation of body fluid volume and blood pressure. If an outlet valve is attached to a tank whose base area is the reciprocal of the total peripheral resistance (TPR) and water is poured into this tank at a rate corresponding to the amount of Na+ absorbed, then equilibrium must be achieved at a certain water level, volume and flow rate of the outlet, which represent the mean arterial pressure (MAP), cardiac output (CO) and urinary excretion of Na+. The height of the outlet from the bottom of the reservoir and the size of the outlet cross-section correspond to the y-intercept and slope of the renal function (pressure-natriuresis) curve. In sodium-sensitive hypertension, due to the shift of the curve to a higher blood pressure level (high outlet height) without a change in the slope (outlet size), and in sodium hypertension, due to the lowered slope of the curve (reduced outlet size), not only the MAP (water level) but also the CO (water volume) are increased, resulting in sodium-retaining hypertension, if the TPR (reverse surface area of base) remains unchanged, while CO is unchanged, leading to sodium hypertension. maintain hypertension, if TPR is elevated. Thus, MAP and its sensitivity to sodium intake are determined by the renal function curve. Since body fluid volume is determined by both the renal function curve and TPR, changes in TPR during the development of hypertension are a major factor in determining whether or not body fluid volume should change a small amount or a large amount. Therefore, sodium sensitivity of blood pressure and sodium retention must be considered separately.

source: Usefulness of frozen section lymph node assessment in the staging of bronchogenic carcinoma during mediastinoscopy. We conducted an analysis of the utility of frozen section diagnostics in determining lymph node status at mediastinoscopy in 122 consecutive patients with bronchogenic carcinoma. Thirty-five of 122 patients had multiple lymph nodes with frozen section evaluation positive for metastatic carcinoma. Subsequent lymph node sections not included in the original frozen section study revealed metastatic carcinoma in two additional patients. The false negative rate was 1.6%. The sensitivity was 94.6%. The predictive value of negative frozen section evaluation results was 97.7%. As there were no false-positive frozen section results, the specificity and predictive value of positive frozen section results was 100%. The status of the lymph nodes of these 122 patients was also evaluated. Six hundred and twenty lymph nodes were collected from the mediastinum during mediastinoscopy. Frozen sections of lymph nodes were positive. Subsequent lymph node sections not included in the frozen section examination revealed metastatic carcinoma in four additional lymph nodes. The false negative rate was 0.6%. The sensitivity was 92.2%. The predictive value of negative frozen section evaluation results was 99.3%. As there were no positive frozen section results, the specificity and predictive value of positive frozen section results was 100%. We conclude that evaluation of lymph nodes by frozen section during mediastinoscopy reliably indicates the status of the lymph nodes, allowing the physician to decide whether or not to proceed with thoracotomy. Carcinoma staging and definitive surgery can be performed in a single anesthetic procedure. The combination of mediastinoscopy and thoracotomy with frozen section diagnostic monitoring reduces both the length and cost of hospitalization.

source: Perforation of the gallbladder: cholescintigraphic and ultrasound results of the Niemeier classification. source: The metabolic consequences of “washed” cardiopulmonary bypass pump priming fluid in children undergoing cardiac operations. The substrate load of the pump priming fluid, particularly glucose and lactate, has a major influence on the metabolic response of children during cardiac operations and may be neurological. It is possible to clean the priming fluid of these excess substrates by ultrafiltration followed by the addition of a balanced electrolyte solution. We used this technique in the management of the bypass surgery of nine children over 1 year old and weighing less than 18 kg who were studied from the induction of anesthesia until 6 hours postoperatively. Frequent blood samples were taken to measure electrolytes, intermediate metabolites, and stress-related hormones. Throughout the study period, electrolyte concentrations were maintained within physiological limits and changes in blood glucose and lactate were minimized compared to those in matched historical controls from previous studies. A preventable cause of postischemic myocardial depression.  
Reperfusion of warm blood cardioplegic solution is useful to minimize reperfusion damage after ischemia.  
This study tests the hypothesis that overzealous administration of cardioplegic blood solution during reperfusion counteracts these benefits and may lead to a prevalence of depressed ventricular performance and mortality similar to that observed after normal blood reperfusion.  
Thirty-one dogs underwent global ischemia at 37°C for 45 minutes on a ventilated bypass.  
Six received normal blood reperfusion and 25 were reperfused with warm aspartate/glutamate-enriched cardioplegic blood solution; of these, eight received a high dose (3,600 +/- 600 ml) and 17 received limited-dose cardioplegic blood reperfusion (1,180 +/- 120 ml) over a period of 10 to 20 minutes.  
High-dose cardioplegic blood perfusion (5,100 +/- 200 ml) without prior ischemia was tested in five additional dogs.  
High-dose blood cardioplegia without prior ischemia did not impair ventricular function (stroke peak work index 96% of control).  
After ischemia, reperfusion (no cardioplegia) resulted in left ventricular dysfunction (peak stroke work index 36% of control, p less than 0.05 compared to control) and a mortality rate of 33% (2/6 died).  
High-dose cardioplegic reperfusion resulted in recovery of stroke work index (40% of control, p less than 0.05 vs. control) and a mortality rate of 25% (2/8 died).  
In contrast, limited-dose reperfusion of cardioplegic blood solution allowed 100% survival (17/17) and restored the stroke work index to 90% of control (1.3 versus 1.45 gm.m/kg).  
We conclude that reperfusion damage can be avoided by initial reoxygenation with limited doses of substrate-enriched blood cardioplegic solution.  
Conversely, high-dose reperfusion of cardioplegic blood solution negates this benefit, reduces recovery, and can be fatal.

source: Capillary Hemangiomas and Flash Lamp-Pumped Pulsed Dye Laser Treatment Strawberry hemangiomas, or capillaries, are common neoplasms, with an incidence of approximately 2.6% in newborns. Treatments such as cryosurgery, irradiation, radium instillation, corticosteroid therapy or surgical excision are ineffective or result in significant morbidity. We describe 10 children with hemangiomas treated with the flash lamp-pumped pulsed dye laser. Patients were 7 weeks old at the start of laser treatment. Patients underwent 3.1 +/- 1 laser treatments, with an average lesion regression of 69.9% +/- 4.5%. PURPOSE: The prognostic significance of pretreatment bone marrow cytogenetic studies in adults with acute lymphocytic leukemia treated at a single institution, with a treatment program, is described. PATIENTS AND METHODS: A total of 105 patients with a documented morphological diagnosis of acute lymphocytic leukemia were examined for this analysis. All patients underwent a thorough workup at presentation and cytogenetic analysis was performed in 103 patients, using the Giemsa strip technique with trypsin pretreatment on cells in 24-hour culture. RESULTS: The specific cytogenetic classification in the 103 patients who had the karyotypic analysis was as follows: diploid 27%; Philadelphia chromosome positive 13%; hyperdiploid 12%; B cell karyotype 6%; 6r- and 14q+ anomalies 4%; pseudodiploid 8%; hypodiploid 2%; and insufficient metaphases 28%. B-cell, 6q- or 14q+, and Philadelphia chromosome-positive karyotypes tended to be correlated with other known negative prognostic factors. Patients with diploid, hyperdiploid, pseudodiploid and hypodiploid karyotypes or with insufficient metaphases could be grouped into a single group with a favorable prognosis. In this group, the remission rate with induction chemotherapy was 89%, the median duration of complete remission was 26 months, and the median survival was 25 months, with a 3-year survival rate of 45%. Patients with positive Philadelphia chromosome, B cell, and 6q- or 14q+ abnormalities collectively had an unfavorable prognosis. Their response rate to induction chemotherapy was 65%, the median duration of response was 7 months, and the median survival was 8 months, with a 3-year survival rate of less than 10%. CONCLUSION: We conclude that pretreatment bone marrow karyotype is an important part of the evaluation of adults with acute lymphocytic leukemia and provides prognostic information.

The Wilms' Tumor Study (NWTS) was initiated in 1969.  
One of its objectives was to modulate treatments according to risk factors in order to minimize the number and severity of iatrogenic complications linked to treatment.  
The NWTS therefore incorporated a follow-up study (LTFS) into its framework to monitor late effects.  
The LTFS is limited to survivors living 5 years or more after initial surgery, and data are collected using specially designed forms.  
A total of 787 patients enrolled in NWTS-1 or NWTS-2 (1969 to 1979) were eligible, of whom 680 were available for analysis regarding their musculoskeletal, cardiovascular, and neuropsychological status, as well as the presence of benign and malignant tumors.  
Patients with disease treated with radiation therapy experienced scoliosis, as well as other musculoskeletal abnormalities (32 versus 2), almost seven times more often than members of the cohort population who did not receive radiation therapy (35 of 57 versus 5 of 53, respectively).  
The difference in cardiovascular problems recorded among survivors who did or did not receive Adriamycin (Adria Laboratories, Columbus, OH) (2.4 versus 1.1 per 100 person-years at risk) was of borderline significance (P = 0.06).  
No excess neuropsychological events were reported in people who received vincristine.  
When considering patients with disease at all stages, malignancies occurred in all 623 patients who underwent radiotherapy (RT patients); benign tumors were also more common in RT patients than in patients who did not receive radiotherapy (41 of 486 or 8% versus 4 of 194 or 2%).  
Continued study of this unique patient body is necessary, particularly for those receiving Adriamycin, due to the known interval required for latent cardiomyopathy to manifest clinically in some patients.

Lingual exfoliative cytology samples (scrapings) were obtained from 18 human immunodeficiency virus-positive patients with oral hairy leukoplakia. Mucosal scrapings were obtained in 12 of these patients. Specimens were processed for examination by transmission microscopy (TEM). Sixteen (89%) of the samples revealed infection of keratinocytes with a herpes-like virus. There was no evidence of infection in the 12 oral mucosal scrapings. Hyphae were observed by TEM in 14 (78%) of the lingual scrapings and two (17%) of the buccal scrapings. One specimen and two biopsy specimens were stained for Epstein-Barr virus DNA with a DNA probe. The detection of herpes-type virions by TEM in the keratinocytes of a lesion suspected of being hairy leukoplakia allows a direct and objective diagnosis. In addition, the use of exfoliative cytological samples constitutes a simple and non-invasive technique.
